q: What total score on the 2010 ACR/EULAR RA classification criteria defines "definite RA"?
explanation:
As printed in Table 101-1, a score greater than 6 classifies definite rheumatoid arthritis (p1608).

A. Exactly 5 total points: Five is the table score for more than 10 involved joints including a small joint, not its printed definite-disease threshold (p1608).
B. Exactly 3 total points: Three is a component score, not the printed total-score threshold for definite disease (p1608).
C. Exactly 2 total points: Two is a component score for 1-3 small joints, not the printed definite-disease threshold (p1608).

q: How useful is anti-CCP antibody testing for distinguishing LORA from polymyalgia rheumatica?
o: One small study found the same positivity in LORA, PMR and healthy older controls
One small study found positivity in 65% of PMR but none of LORA or healthy controls
One small study found positivity in every LORA patient and none of the PMR patients
One small study found positivity in 65% of LORA but none of PMR or healthy controls
explanation:
In one small study, anti-CCP was positive in 65% of LORA patients but none of the PMR patients or healthy older controls, suggesting usefulness as a discriminator (p1611).

B. One small study found positivity in 65% of PMR but none of LORA or healthy controls: The 65% result belongs to LORA, not PMR (p1611).
C. One small study found positivity in every LORA patient and none of the PMR patients: The LORA result was 65%, not universal positivity (p1611).
A. One small study found the same positivity in LORA, PMR and healthy older controls: The groups differed: 65% in LORA and none in the other two groups (p1611).

q: What RA-specific risk requires evaluation before intubating a patient with long-standing disease?
o: Protection of the cervical spine by long-standing RA
Overextension as a means to prevent spinal-cord compromise
Absence of cervical risk after more than 10 years of RA
Cervical spine disease and atlantoaxial joint instability
explanation:
Long-standing RA can cause cervical spine disease and atlantoaxial instability, making overextension during intubation hazardous (p1612).

A. Protection of the cervical spine by long-standing RA: The book describes increased risk of cervical disease and instability (p1612).
C. Absence of cervical risk after more than 10 years of RA: More than 10 years of RA is identified as a particular risk setting (p1612).
B. Overextension as a means to prevent spinal-cord compromise: Overextension can compromise the brainstem or spinal cord (p1612).

q: How much more likely are Sjögren syndrome patients to develop lymphoma compared to matched controls?
o: Two to five times more likely
explanation:
Patients with Sjogren syndrome are 44 times more likely to develop lymphoma than matched normal subjects (p1626).

A. Two to five times more likely: This is the hematologic-malignancy risk in RA (p1626).
C. Two times more likely: This is the lymphoma risk with azathioprine or cyclosporin in RA relative to RA controls (p1626).
B. 50 times more likely: This is the non-Hodgkin lymphoma incidence in renal-transplant patients (p1626).
